bullets.title: Fed Decision Today: ~30% Market Odds of Surprise Hike; Warsh Messaging in Focus
bullets.body: Markets price a 30-33% probability of a 25bp hike (SOFR at 32%, CME FedWatch 24%), with the base case a hawkish hold at 3.5-3.75%. Fed Chair Warsh's silence ahead of the meeting has amplified uncertainty; JPM models ~2 hawkish dissents. Scenarios: hawkish hold = -25bp to +50bp SPX reaction; dovish hold = best outcome at +50bp to +1%.

bullets.title: Middle East Escalation: Iran Fires Ballistic Missiles, Oil Surges 4-5%
bullets.body: Iran's IRGC launched multiple ballistic missiles at U.S. bases in Jordan at 5:45pm ET; all were intercepted per CENTCOM. U.S. and Saudi Arabia struck Iran-backed logistics in Iraq. WTI surged 4.5-5% to $82-83/bbl overnight after a 3-day, 16% decline. Chile's central bank flagged renewed Middle East risk on oil supply. Qatar LNG force majeure and elevated war-risk premiums add inflation pressure beyond crude.

bullets.title: KOSPI Circuit-Breaker Crash: Down 10-13%, De-leveraging ~90% Complete
bullets.body: South Korea's KOSPI fell as much as 12.6%, triggering circuit breakers on consecutive days and tracking for its worst monthly loss ever (~30-35% MTD). JPM estimates the Korean de-leveraging cycle is ~90% complete; leveraged ETF AUM normalized from $50B to $17B and HF L/S ratios dropped from 5.7x to 3.2x. Finance minister Koo convened an emergency market meeting and apologized for introducing leveraged ETFs. Bank of England is probing Asian equity risk at prime brokers.

bullets.title: AI/Momentum Unwind: Worst Month for Semis Since 2002; HF De-grossing at Record Pace
bullets.body: Semiconductors are down ~22.5% MTD, on pace for their worst month since December 2002. Goldman's High Beta Momentum index erased all YTD gains after a 41% drawdown—the worst monthly momentum performance on record (ex-COVID). Asia-focused fundamental L/S managers are down 18.6% MTD, the largest monthly drawdown on record; global prime book saw its largest single-day de-grossing since Sept 2025 (-3 SD) on July 27. JPM's positioning monitor now flashing a buy signal.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler Capex Credibility Test: MSFT & META Report Tonight; AI Bubble Debate Intensifies
bullets.body: MSFT faces the worst sentiment in Mag-7 heading into earnings; investors want tangible Copilot/LLM monetization proof with FY27 capex guidance a key focus ($230-280B median). META expected to guide capex higher for 2026. Jefferies warns AI capex cycle is approaching a critical inflection: big-tech capex of ~$900B in 2026 and ~$1.4T in 2027 requires $2.5T annual revenue to break even per The Economist, versus only ~$150B current AI revenues. CDS for MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META have all widened to record levels for IG names.

bullets.title: Broader Market Rotation: Equal-Weight S&P at Record, Small Caps Outperforming; Tech Lagging
bullets.body: While the Nasdaq 100 is near correction territory, the equal-weight S&P 500 outperformed the cap-weighted index by ~100bp on Tuesday and hit record highs. 72% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 200-day MA (strongest breadth since Dec 2024). Capital is rotating into Financials, Healthcare, and Cyclicals and away from mega-cap tech. Piper notes this rotation theme is intact.

bullets.title: Semiconductor Earnings: STX Massive Beat-and-Raise; KLAC/VRT/NXPI Mixed
bullets.body: STX crushed estimates with F4Q revenue of $3.63B (vs $3.50B Street) and guided F1Q to $4.1B / EPS $7.30 (vs $5.89 Street); pricing power accelerates to +20% YoY in F1Q27 with nearline capacity allocated into CY28. KLAC guided F1Q to $4.0B—above Street but below elevated buy-side bar—stock fell ~8% premarket; WFE raised to low-$150B. VRT -15% on weaker-than-expected margins. NXPI beat but lacked auto upside vs. elevated expectations, shares fell.

bullets.title: SK Hynix Misses Elevated Expectations Despite 557% Profit Surge; Memory Cycle Concerns
bullets.body: SK Hynix Q2 operating profit of KRW 60.54T missed consensus KRW 64.22T despite 557% YoY growth; revenue of KRW 79T missed KRW 83-84T estimates. The miss was driven by HBM product mix/timing rather than a demand breakdown; management guided for stronger H2 with HBM4 ramps boosting ASPs. U.S. memory proxy MU fell on read-through. Korean stock market amplified the reaction through leveraged ETF de-risking.

bullets.title: Trump Admin Bans Chinese Robots and Power Inverters to Protect AI Supply Chain
bullets.body: The Trump administration announced bans on imports of new Chinese humanoid robots, quadruped robots, and connected power inverters effective Tuesday, citing AI supply chain and cybersecurity risks. The FCC's inverter ban (all foreign-produced new models) is seen as immediately positive for U.S. solar inverter makers. Chinese AI model imports are also being discussed as a potential future target.

bullets.title: Oil Volatile: 16% Three-Day Collapse Then 4-5% Reversal on Iran Attack
bullets.body: Brent crude fell ~16% in three sessions to $84/bbl as Iran-US tensions appeared to cool, then reversed sharply overnight (Brent +4.8%, WTI +4.5% to $82-83) after Iran's IRGC ballistic missile attack on Jordan. U.S. API crude inventory data showed a 3.3M bbl build vs. a -2.5M estimate. Chile's central bank cited renewed Middle East oil risk in holding its policy rate.

bullets.title: Fed Chair Warsh Internal Friction: Waller, Barr, Bostic Resisting Proposed Changes
bullets.body: Sources report Fed Governor Waller has been publicly critical of Chair Warsh at meetings; Governor Barr is opposing balance sheet modifications before formal proposals; Atlanta Fed's Bostic is concerned about ad-hoc policy changes. The internal divisions increase uncertainty around today's statement language and dissent count.

bullets.title: Euro Area Growth Tracking ~1.5%; Wage Growth Stable Near 2.6-2.7%
bullets.body: Euro area growth is running at ~1.5% annualized, boosted by a 16.6% q/q Irish GDP surge that adds ~0.5 percentage points; ex-Ireland growth is ~1.0%. ECB wage tracker shows 2.6% YoY growth in 2H, rising to ~2.7% in early 2027—slightly above firm expectations. Belgium GDP stagnated, tilting regional risks to the downside.

bullets.title: Sector Rotation into Healthcare and Away from AI Infrastructure Accelerating
bullets.body: Hedgeye reports healthcare (XLV) +2.4% vs. tech (XLK) -10.1% on the month; REITs (XLRE) +4.5% in July. JPM's morning briefing flagged healthcare as positioned for a durable inflection with attractive valuations and 2027 earnings upside. Financials, healthcare, and cyclicals are all in early-stage uptrends per UBS; S&P target range 7,515-8,620.

bullets.title: AI Capex Credibility: GPU Spot Pricing Firm, But CDS at Records Reflect Market Uncertainty
bullets.body: Spot GPU compute pricing remains significantly above contracted rates, suggesting hyperscalers are underearning and OCF acceleration is an underappreciated funding source (one analyst argues the market is overreacting to CDS widening). However, ORCL 5yr CDS hit 215bps (vs 144bps YTD) after an S&P downgrade to BBB-; NVDA and GOOGL CDS also at records. Investors waiting for MSFT capex guidance and META capex commentary tonight as potential sentiment floor for tech trade.

bullets.title: Broad Earnings Backdrop: Consumer Resilient (Visa, Ford); Staples Mixed (PG Weak)
bullets.body: Visa Q3 US payments volume grew 10% YoY (best since pre-COVID 2019) with cross-border +13% and VAS +34%; July volumes softening. Ford raised FY26 adj. EBIT to $10-11B (from $8.5-10.5B) despite $1B higher aluminum costs and BlueOval charges. PG 4Q organic sales flat vs. +1.6% expected; FY27 guidance brackets Street but weaker exit rate concerns investors; UBS expects ~3.5% downside.

bullets.title: Japan Kumamoto Earthquake: TSMC Japan Evacuated, Renesas and Sony Fabs Halted
bullets.body: A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck Kumamoto; TSMC evacuated its Japan fab, confirmed structural integrity, and workers have returned to inspect lines. Renesas halted two Kumamoto facilities and is reviewing equipment damage. Sony Semiconductor's Kumamoto fab remains suspended. Toyota initially halted then restarted three Kyushu factories.

bullets.title: U.S. M2 at Record $23.15T; Retail Traffic Decelerating in July
bullets.body: U.S. M2 hit a new all-time high of $23.155T. Separately, Citi's retail traffic tracker shows July MTD traffic +2.2% YoY vs. June's +2.5%, continuing a deceleration trend; 2Q26 was +1.9% vs. 1Q26 +3.3%. Citi CC spending data shows July MTD retail spending -1.7% (hard comparison to July '25) but 2Q26 accelerating vs. 1Q26.

bullets.title: FCC Power Inverter Ban Positive for U.S. Solar Names; Chinese Robot Import Ban Announced
bullets.body: FCC banned all foreign-produced power inverters (new models only), immediately benefiting ENPH, SEDG, and NXT in the U.S. C&I market. ENPH's base case upside is ~50MW (~$15-90M incremental annual revenue). Separately, the Trump admin banned Chinese humanoid and quadruped robot imports to protect U.S. AI supply chain integrity—domestic humanoid robotics companies seen as beneficiaries.
